channel.title: ChiChieh Huang
channel.description: Essays on generative AI, AI agents and agent memory, translated from Traditional Chinese.

item.title: I Switched My Main Machine to a 9950X So 33 Subagents Could Run at Once
item.description: My agents now send out up to 33 subagents at once, and my R7 7700 kept freezing Windows under the load. Upgrading to a Ryzen 9 9950X finally made local agent work smooth again.

item.title: Anthropic's IPO Filing Warns About Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: Anthropic's S-1/A warns that future models may soon speed up AI R&D on their own. Here's why that risk factor reads like a flex, and whether a public company with a ~$895B compute bill could really hit pause.

item.title: Speaking at AI Impact Day in the Data Village
item.description: A short note after speaking about AI memory at AI Impact Day, on how hard it was to explain the idea to a general audience, and on a November packed with talks.

item.title: Can an Agent Learn to Manage Its Own Memory?
item.description: Remembering correctly isn't enough if the agent can't pick, tidy and weigh its notes. What recent research says about learned memory policies, and how to test them against the next real task.

item.title: My Old Gaming PCs Are Now CI Runners
item.description: AI agents made my PRs so fast that CI became the bottleneck and GitHub Actions got expensive, so I pulled my twelve-year-old gaming PC and other old machines back into service as a home CI pool.

item.title: Last Year I Learned to Look Up at the Vision, This Year to Look Down at My Feet
item.description: A clear ten-year vision kept our team steady while we pivoted to Cairn, but it couldn't tell me what to build next. What reference points, adoption stages and segmentation taught me about focus.

item.title: When Memory Gets Attacked
item.description: Memory poisoning turns an agent's own notes against it. A made-up discount case shows how a claim becomes "policy," and how to separate notes from rules, gate actions, clean up and test.

item.title: When You Can Take Your ChatGPT Subscription With You, How Does the AI Product Business Change?
item.description: OpenAI now lets ChatGPT Plus and Pro users spend their plan's usage inside third-party tools. Here is what that means for pricing AI products, choosing models and OpenAI's own moat.

item.title: Jev Lab: Deciding What an Agent Should Remember
item.description: A small experiment using Jev to decide whether a candidate memory should be kept at all, compared with Luna across 100 synthetic cases, and what filtering does to the next answer.

item.title: Remembering Isn't the Same as Remembering Right
item.description: Once an agent stops forgetting, the next problem is whether it keeps remembering wrong. How to build reliability into writing, updating and reading memory, and how to test that it actually worked.

item.title: How Agent Memory Forms, Updates and Fades
item.description: Memory isn't a static snapshot. It has a lifecycle of formation, evolution and retrieval, with consolidation, updating and forgetting in between. The season one finale of my Agent Memory series.

item.title: Everyone Talks About Memory. Do We Mean the Same Thing?
item.description: Everyone working on AI agents talks about memory, but chat history, MEMORY.md, RAG, context engineering and fine-tuning answer different questions. The first essay in my Agent Memory series pulls them apart.

item.title: What Should an Agent Remember?
item.description: Not everything that happens is worth an agent remembering. Factual, experiential and working memory each do a different job, and stacking them against memory's form gives you a map of the field.

item.title: Talking About Cairn at the Taiwan AI Annual Conference, I Found Everyone Falls into the Same Pothole
item.description: A thank-you note after my talk on agent memory at the 2026 Taiwan AI Annual Conference, and what I heard there: many teams keep losing what they learn in AI sessions and re-solving the same bugs.

item.title: What Does an Agent's Memory Actually Look Like?
item.description: Where an agent's memory lives and what form it takes are two different questions. A tour of token-level, parametric and latent memory, and where MEMORY.md, vector DBs and knowledge graphs fit.

item.title: MCP Goes Stateless: Getting Ready for Scale
item.description: The July 2026 MCP stable release removes protocol-level sessions, adds multi round-trip requests and moves extra capabilities into extensions. What changes, what doesn't, and whether to upgrade now.

item.title: Coming Up at the Taiwan AI Annual Conference: Keeping the Lessons from AI Sessions for Your Team
item.description: A preview of my talk at the 2026 Taiwan AI Annual Conference on Cairn, which turns debugging lessons and design decisions buried in individual AI sessions into shared team memory.

item.title: AWS Summit × Agile Taipei: Two Packed Talks on Agent Memory
item.description: Two back-to-back talks on agent memory at AWS Summit Taipei and Agile Taipei, both packed, and why team-level memory is a different problem from personal memory.

item.title: Productizing MCP: Where to Draw the Line as Tools Pile Up
item.description: Once MCP goes to production, the hard problem isn't connecting tools but deciding how much an LLM should see. Context, exposure and orchestration, and the agent-backed MCP tool pattern.

item.title: Employee, Assistant or Tool? How Three Agent Frameworks Really Differ
item.description: Claude Code, OpenClaw and Hermes Agent look similar on a feature list, but they define an agent differently at the root. Following their memory design shows who each one thinks the agent is.
